headline: Approved Board of Ethics appointments of Jane Fisher and Maria Harlow, plus consent items including $4,104.34 in tax refunds.
summary: Councilors approved a set of consent agenda items, including tax refunds, police donations, and bid waivers for electric work. They also approved the appointments of Jane Fisher and Maria Harlow to the Board of Ethics by a 7-0 roll call vote, after discussion of recusal rules. Residents also raised questions about sidewalk repairs, contaminated soil at 60 Prince Street, and the future of the high schools.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items 3a through 3i and 3l, including tax refunds and bid waivers, by voice vote with all present councilors voting aye.
Approved the appointments of Jane Fisher and Maria Harlow as regular members of the Board of Ethics, for terms expiring October 19, 2029, by a 7-0 roll call vote with 2 absent.

4. Items Removed from the Consent Agenda 
 
Councilor Tatta requested that items 3j and 3k be removed from the Consent Agenda.  She would like to 
discuss the process of appointments to the Board of Ethics for people who have or may potentially have 
ties with other town organizations, creating a conflict of interest.  Appointments to the Board of Ethics 
are determined by the Mayor. 
 
The Mayor explained the Board of Ethics are bound by the Code of Ethics.  If there is a conflict or 
concern, they have an obligation to recuse themselves from the item being discussed.  Alternates are 
assigned to the Board for this purpose.  The Mayor was asked if he feels the ordinance sufficiently lays 
out the issues that a member would need to recuse themselves.  Mayor answered that a breach of ethics 
is a breach of ethics, whether by the Board of Ethics or the Town Council.  The code of ethics is 
universal and if a member has a conflict on something being discussed, the member should recuse 
themselves. 
 
Councilor Laffin supports having local community members involved in these positions as they are part 
of the fabric of Wallingford and can recuse themselves just as the Town Council can recuse themselves 
from council duties. 
 
Councilor Rivard feels that most of the people of the highest character in Wallingford are already 
engaged with the town government.  If we make it challenging for these members to be appointed due to

potential conflicts, we may lose good candidates that have already demonstrated good character and 
high ethical standards. 
 
Councilor Rossacci feels we should break away from doing things the way we’ve always done them.  
The Board of Ethics is a five (5) person committee.  We should be able to find five (5) ethical people 
that do not receive money from the town.  She supports the reappointment of Jane Fisher and Maria 
Harlow. 
 
Chairman Testa would support the Ordinance Committee reviewing this ordinance to specify the terms a 
member would need to recuse themselves. 
 
Bill Comerford, Broadview Drive, would like to see the Charter reviewed and feels that the Board of 
Ethics should be made up of members that reside in surrounding towns, such as Cheshire or Southington 
to ensure board members will be impartial.

5. PUBLIC QUESTION & ANSWER PERIOD 
 
Sheila Tierney stated it’s been 28 weeks since money was appropriated to replace the Parade Ground 
driveway because of crumbling concrete and tripping hazards.  Since then, she has submitted 36 
investigation reports for sidewalk repair to the Engineering Department and only two (2) have been 
investigated.    She is asking for the Engineering Department to paint the areas that are tripping hazards.  
She feels there are other roads that should have been addressed earlier and are in worse disrepair than 
the Parade Grounds.   
 
Bill Comerford read a statement regarding contaminated soil at 60 Prince Street.  He asked for an 
environmental audit of 60 Prince St and the cemetery road. 
 
Jim Economopoulos spoke in regard to the poor condition of both high schools.  He would like the issue 
of having one (1) or two (2) high schools resolved so we can either work on repairing/rehabbing both 
schools or constructing one (1) high school for Wallingford.  This is a long-standing issue that needs to 
be resolved. 
 
Chairman Testa agreed to put this topic on the next meeting agenda for follow up. 
 
6. Consider and approve the naming of softball field #1 at Pragemann Park after Stanley 
Shepardson –Parks & Recreation 
 
Item 6 was previously removed from the agenda and will be represented at a future meeting. 
 
7. Discussion of the June 2026 reports from the Comptroller summarizing the Unaudited Municipal     
           Account for end of fiscal year 2025-2026 – Councilor Reynolds  
 
Councilor Reynolds requested to examine the relationship between the unaudited General Expense 
Summary Report and the unaudited General Fund Revenue Report to determine if departments met their 
goals. There was a discussion on encumbrances, expenses and revenue.  Comptroller Tim Sena 
explained that the budget is a road map of what we can spend and department heads make their best 
guess on what will be used.  His job is to ensure that the departments don’t spend more than what is 
allotted to them. Mayor spoke about the importance of keeping a good bond rating so we can borrow 
money as inexpensively as possible. 
 
Councilor Tatta inquired about a Finance software system that would provide historical data and trends 
on previous budgets as well as the status of direct deposit to employees.  Mr. Sena explained it’s been 
difficult to implement but they are working on it. 
 
Councilor Rivard feels we need to think about bonding for future projects. 
 
Jason Michael asked for the final number on the police station.  Mr. Sena explained there is not a final 
number yet.  There is a final invoice that needs to be paid.

Sheila Tierney inquired as to which roads were paved using the $390,136 paving funds in the budget.  
She contacted Public Works and was told ten (10) roads were paved in the Spring and there will not be 
paving in the Fall.  The remainder of the $390,136 was returned to the Cap and Non Fund. 
 
8.  Chairman’s Update 
 
(a) Golden Fox Theatre  
 
Chairman Testa requested an update from the Mayor.  Mayor stated he received a response to his email 
from Mr. Michael and will follow up.  Mr. Michael addressed the Council to clarify he responded to the 
Mayor’s email that he would meet with the Mayor to discuss facility usage and storage but he will not 
create another budget.  He feels the Council approved the $5000 grant funds and he should be awarded 
them.
